from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Reynolds Number measures inertia versus viscous forces.",
            "Turbulence emerges when thresholds are exceeded.",
            "This triggers a cascade of energy."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Language of Flux", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Reynolds Number formula
        re_formula = MathTex(r"R_e = \frac{\text{inertia}}{\text{viscous}}", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(re_formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(re_formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fluid icon and turbulence
        fluid_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fluid.svg")
        fluid_icon.set_color("#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(fluid_icon, 'E3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(fluid_icon))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Cascade visualization (circles of different sizes)
        cascade = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color="#00BFFF").shift(DOWN*0.5*i + RIGHT*0.5*i) for i in range(3)])
        self.place_at_grid(cascade, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(cascade))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00BFFF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Turbulence follows strict statistical laws.",
            "The 5/3 law represents turbulent DNA.",
            "Energy dissipation defines the cascade limit."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        stat_law = Text("Statistical Laws", font_size=36)
        dna_curve = MathTex(r"E(k) \propto k^{-5/3}", font_size=42)
        dissipation = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        dissipation_label = Text("Dissipation", font_size=24)
        dissipation_group = VGroup(dissipation, dissipation_label).arrange(DOWN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(stat_law, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(stat_law), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(stat_law.animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(dna_curve, 'C4')
        self.play(Write(dna_curve), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(dna_curve.animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(dissipation_group, 'E3')
        self.play(Create(dissipation), Write(dissipation_label), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.play(dissipation.animate.set_color("#00BFFF"), dissipation_label.animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Language of Flux
sections.content: Establish the Reynolds Number (Re) as the dimensionless ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces. Explain that turbulence emerges when Re exceeds a critical threshold, leading to energy cascade.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Honey vs. Water' experiment: Honey (low Re) flows in smooth layers; water (high Re) breaks into chaotic eddies.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Hypothesis: Self-Similarity
sections.content: Introduce Kolmogorov’s 1941 theory (K41). Explain the 'Energy Cascade' where large eddies break into smaller ones until viscous dissipation dominates. Define the Kolmogorov length scale (η) and time scale (τ).
sections.example: An animation of a large 'Whirlpool' splitting into smaller circles, showing that statistics are the same regardless of scale (fractal-like behavior).

sections.title: The Mathematical Structure: The 5/3 Law
sections.content: Derive the Power Spectrum E(k) ~ C * ε^(2/3) * k^(-5/3). Define ε (dissipation rate) and C (Kolmogorov constant, ~1.5). Focus on the 'inertial subrange' where viscosity is negligible.
sections.example: A graph plotting log(Energy) vs log(Wavenumber). Show a distinct '-5/3' slope line superimposed over the curve of a turbulent smoke plume.

sections.title: Application: Turbulence in Nature
sections.content: Connect the math to real-world energy distribution. Discuss why this statistical predictability matters for aerodynamics and climate modeling.
sections.example: A 'Peregrine Falcon' diving: The bird manages turbulent air pockets by utilizing the energy cascade to stabilize its trajectory at high velocities.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap: Turbulence is not truly random; it follows statistical laws dictated by the constant C and the energy dissipation rate ε. The -5/3 law is the 'DNA' of turbulent flow.
sections.example: A quick visual loop summarizing the scale transition from macro (large eddies) to micro (dissipation) as a final 'big picture' slide.
